baseline

Baseline torch.geqrf loops cuSOLVER serially over the batch (640x512 = 1.07s); the entire game is batched parallelism. Write a CUSTOM blocked compact-WY Householder QR (Triton): factor a width-32/64 column panel per matrix (unblocked Householder, build T via T3=-T1(Y1^T Y2)T2), then apply the trailing update A:=(I-VTV^T)A as a TENSOR-CORE batched GEMM across all matrices at once. This natively emits geqrf's (H,tau) packing: R on/above diag, reflectors below, tau separate. Target the n=512/1024 large-batch shapes. Get FP32-correct first (rank-deficient cases are a hard gate), then try TF32 internally and re-verify. Validate on the large B=640 ranked shapes, not just test shapes.

Blocked compact-WY Householder QR, PyTorch batched, FP32 trailing GEMM. All 22 tests pass. B=640 n=512 shapes 4.8-5.0x faster than baseline (223k vs 1076k us); but small/few-matrix shapes (n=32/176/352/2048/4096) much slower due to per-column Python launch overhead. Geomean 241673 us (worse than baseline 131456 due to small shapes).

Fused panel geqr2 into a single Triton kernel (one program per matrix, BLOCK_L x BLOCK_IB register tile, on-chip column loop). Collapsed ~30k tiny launches to ~3/panel. All 22 tests pass. Geomean 31832us = 4.1x vs baseline 131456. B=640 n=512 shapes 28-30x faster (37k vs 1076k us). Laggards: low-batch large-n (n=2048 B=8: 2.1x slower; n=4096 B=2: 12x slower) due to poor occupancy of one-program-per-matrix panel + small trailing GEMM batch.

Fused T-formation (dlarft recurrence on-chip from resident V) and clean unit-trapezoidal V output into the panel kernel. Eliminated the form_T Python loop (~500 tiny gemv) and Vmask reconstruction+clone. All 22 tests pass. Geomean 8157us = 16.1x vs baseline. B=640 n=512 now 12.9k us (83.6x faster). Remaining laggards: n=2048 B=8 (115k us) and n=4096 B=2 (734k us) -- one-program-per-matrix panel has ~2-8 CTA occupancy and huge register tiles for large n.

Tuned panel kernel num_warps by tile height (4/8/16/32 for BLOCK_L <256/>=256/>=2048/>=4096) to cut register spilling on tall panels. n=4096 B=2 734k->176k us, n=2048 B=8 115k->46k us. All tests pass. Geomean 6712us = 19.6x vs baseline. Large-n still occupancy-limited (2-8 CTAs, one-program-per-matrix). Next: tensor-core (tf32x3) trailing GEMM for n=512 (27% GEMM time), and multi-CTA cooperative panel for large-n.

Swept panel width nb and made it adaptive: nb=16 for n>=2048 (smaller L x nb register tile = less spilling), nb=32 otherwise. nb=64 worse everywhere, nb=8 worse than 16 (launch overhead). n=2048 45.6k->23.4k, n=4096 175.7k->95k us. All tests pass. Geomean 6038us = 21.8x vs baseline. Large-n still occupancy-bound (B=2-8 -> 2-8 CTAs). Next: multi-CTA cooperative panel or recursive blocking to fill GPU for few-matrix large-n; faster panel kernel for medium n.

Fused the trailing-update rank-k subtract into a single baddbmm (beta=1, alpha=-1) instead of bmm + elementwise subtract. Removed a full-size elementwise kernel per panel. All tests pass. Geomean 5304us = 24.8x vs baseline. n=512 shapes 11.0k, n=1024 9.6k, n=2048 19.5k, n=4096 86.8k us. Panel kernel still dominates large-n (occupancy) and is ~46% of n=512.

Reordered panel kernel to store the panel (R+reflectors) and V before the T-formation loop, so the panel tile dies and frees registers during T. ncu showed panel kernel is register-bound (1 block/SM, 12.5% warp occupancy). Modest gains on larger shapes (n=1024 9.7->8.8ms, n=2048->18.1, n=4096->83.7). All tests pass. Geomean 5130us = 25.6x vs baseline.

APPROACH (worked): right-looking blocked compact-WY Householder QR. Single fused Triton panel kernel per panel (one program/matrix, on-chip geqr2 column loop in honest FP32, builds V + dlarft T on-chip from the resident tile); trailing update C:=(I-V T^T V^T)C as 3 batched cuBLAS GEMMs with the rank-k subtract fused via baddbmm. Emits exact geqrf (H,tau) packing; passes all ill-conditioned/rankdef/clustered/band/rowscale/mixed cases. Key wins in order: fuse geqr2 into one kernel (30k->~3 launches/panel, 4.1x-> then), fuse T+V into panel kernel (16.1x), num_warps by tile height to kill register spill (19.6x), adaptive nb=16 for n>=2048 (21.8x), baddbmm fuse (24.8x), store-panel-early to free regs (25.6x). FAILED/dead-ends: TF32 single-pass trailing GEMM (fails factor residual on band/rowscale/mixed); bf16x3 trailing (8-bit mantissa too lossy, fails rankdef/clustered scaled-resid 24-135); tf32x3 trailing -- ACCURATE (passes all) but my hand Triton batched GEMM is SLOWER than cuBLAS FP32 even autotuned (cuBLAS wins small-batch medium-K); nb=64 worse everywhere. Trailing GEMMs (cuBLAS FP32 simt, no tensor cores) are ~40% of n=512. NEXT-STEP DIRECTIONS for fresh briefs: (1) HIGHEST LEVERAGE: shared-memory panel geqr2 -- put the LxIB tile in smem not registers to lift the 1-block/SM ceiling (competitor's proven path). torch load_inline CUDA is BLOCKED here (torch headers don't compile under gcc-13/nvcc-13.3: List_inl.h 'need typename' error, -fpermissive doesn't fix); use NVRTC (cuda-python nvrtc bindings ARE installed) to compile raw .cu bypassing torch headers, launch via driver API with tensor.data_ptr(). (2) multi-CTA cooperative panel (split tall panel rows across CTAs w/ a global atomic barrier; safe for B=2-8 since grid<=148 SMs) for the n=2048/4096 few-matrix shapes (still 2-8 CTAs today). (3) efficient tf32x3 trailing GEMM (CUTLASS 3xTF32 grouped-GEMM, or cuBLAS BF16x9 emulation on Blackwell) to beat cuBLAS FP32 on the ~40% GEMM time. (4) reduce panel internal full-tile masked-op redundancy via inner sub-blocking with tl.dot. Per-shape now (us): n32=47 n176=434 n352=1121 n512=11.0k x4 n1024=9.6k x3 n2048=19.5k n4096=86.8k -- large-n still dominates local geomean but leaderboard ranks differently (we're #3).

Hybrid panel dispatch + leaner launcher. Adaptive trailing num_warps for the tf32x3 trailing kernels: 2 warps for high-batch shapes (n=512/1024, B>=60) since thousands of (32,64) tiles pack more programs/SM (n512 9132 -2.7%, n1024 8365 -1.4%); 4 warps for low-batch tall shapes (n=2048 B=8, n=4096 B=2) which want more warps/program. Geomean 4612us = 28.5x baseline, BEATS prev 4657. n2048/n4096 held (15709/77087). All 22 tests + diff/invariance guards pass.

Cooperative all-warps reflector build in the smem panel kernel. ncu (n=512) showed qr_panel stall-bound: 35.3% of stall cycles waiting at CTA barriers, Issued Warp/Sched 0.39 -- the old single-warp build left NW-1 warps idle behind a serial O(L/32) norm-reduce + v-write. Now ALL NT threads reduce their stripe of the column norm (warp-shuffle then block-sum via sw) and write their stripe of sv; every thread recomputes the uniform reflector scalars (alpha read before any overwrite, no broadcast). Geomean 4415us = 29.8x baseline, BEATS prev 4612. n1024 7823 (-6.5%), n4096 61112 (-20.7%, 32-warp blocks benefit most), n512 8950 (-2.0%), n2048 flat (Triton). All 22 tests + diff/invariance guards pass.

Register-cache the smem panel apply for L<=512 (the panel is MIO/smem-throughput bound). Cache this lane's sv stripe in registers ONCE (reused for every column the warp owns) and cache each column's stripe across the dot so the axpy reuses both -- eliminates the axpy's smem re-read of sv and colc (the two dominant MIO loads). Static-indexed float[16] arrays (no local-mem spill). Larger panels (L>512) keep the plain 2-read loop since a 128-chunk cache would spill. n512 8804 (-1.6%, 4 dominant shapes), n4096 58041 (-5.0%); n1024 ~flat (1024-thread blocks are register-starved). Geomean 4395us = 29.9x baseline, BEATS prev 4415. All 22 tests + guards pass.

Panel warp count NW=16 for B<64 (was 32). The register-cached apply (iter 6) raised regs/thread to ~60, so a 1024-thread block (NW=32, the old n=1024 setting) is register-starved and spills; 16 warps = 512-thread block gives the cache room. n1024 7627 (-3.2%, all 3 shapes: dense/mixed/nearrank), n4096 flat (trailing-bound), n512 stable. Geomean 4351us = 30.2x baseline, BEATS prev 4395. All 22 tests + diff/invariance guards pass.

(2) tf32x3 ERROR-CORRECTED trailing [77141802, -6%] -- replaced the 3 cuBLAS FP32 simt trailing GEMMs with worker-2's proven 2-kernel tf32x3 Triton split (YT-reduce then V@YT apply); passes ALL ill-conditioned cases, two-kernel split required (fused is leaderboard-rejected). n512 -6.6%, n2048 -13%. (b) sv/colc register-reuse via runtime-indexed ccols[] array SPILLS to local memory (catastrophic, n1024 16k); only STATIC-indexed caches work. (c) T-formation (dlarft) register-cache regresses -- not a big enough fraction to justify +registers, starves the dominant geqr2 apply. (d) nb/NW knob sweeps on n=512/1024 are EXHAUSTED (<1%, mostly negative) -- panel was stall/MIO-bound, not occupancy-bound. Your smem-panel wall is the SERIAL geqr2 rank-1 chain (one-block-per-matrix, smem-limited 3 blocks/SM). CORRECTNESS: every variant passed all 22 tests + diff/invariance guards incl rankdef/clustered/nearrank/nearcollinear/mixed -- the BLAS-3 sub-blocking is numerically sound, it just loses on speed. ROOT CAUSE (ncu on parent n512 panel k=0): STALL-bound at 1.04 eligible warps/scheduler, 3 blocks/SM (smem-limited, sA=L*32=64KB), 60 regs/thread, 4.94 active warps. The stall is the SERIAL reflector-BUILD chain (ib sequential columns, each reflector depends on the prior applied) -- NOT the apply. STAGE 2 (wmma m16n8k8 tf32x3) therefore SKIPPED on principle: no FMA gain to build on + it accelerates the apply, not the serial build wall. RECOMMENDATION: this one-block-per-matrix smem line has a hard floor ~4356us set by the serial per-column reflector build; it cannot be broken by attacking the apply. To go faster you must parallelize the BUILD itself -- which is exactly what worker-2's batch-major line does (same column-k reflector across the whole batch in one launch = the build is data-parallel across 640 matrices), and why batch-major reaches 3627us and is structurally ahead.
